[LSTO.4.7.4] The "startup hydrate" of [LSTO.4.7.1] / [LSTO.4.7.2] is realised at
the integration boundary by the cache-seed operation ([IARC.12] / [NSTG.9]): a
setup-only, direct cache-store write that restores persisted entries before the
engine's first stream event ([NLFC.9.1]). It is **not** a rule's surface — no rule or expression seeds the cache; a rule
writes the cache with `cache` / `cache_delete` and reads it with `cached()`. An
`initial` block's cache item seeds a key as the host's seed does ([LGRA.24.3]). (The `.dstest` `initial: cache`
arrange, [LTSL.5.2], drives the same primitive, but that is test scaffolding, not
the authored program.)
